title: Greeting to the Church in Magnesia
english: Ignatius, who is also called Theophorus, to the church at Magnesia on the Maeander, blessed in the grace of God the Father in Christ Jesus our Savior. In him I greet this church, and I pray that it may have abundant joy in God the Father and in Jesus Christ.
orientation: Ignatius opens his letter to the church in Magnesia with a formal greeting, identifying himself and blessing the church in the name of God the Father and Jesus Christ.

title: Rejoicing in the Magnesians' ordered love and hoping in Christ
english: I have come to know how well ordered your love for God is, and I rejoice greatly. So I have chosen to speak to you in the faith of Jesus Christ.

For I have been deemed worthy of a name most befitting God, and in the chains I carry around I sing to the churches, in which there is unity. I pray for the flesh and spirit of Jesus Christ, who is our life through all things, and for faith and love, than which nothing has been preferred, and for what is more authoritative, Jesus and the Father. If we endure in him every assault of the ruler of this age and escape, we will attain God.
orientation: Ignatius, bishop of Antioch writing as a prisoner on his way to martyrdom in Rome, opens his letter to the church in Magnesia by praising their ordered love and stating his hope in Jesus Christ.

title: Worthy to see the Magnesians through their bishop and clergy
english: So I was counted worthy to see you in the persons of Damas your bishop, who is worthy of God, of your worthy elders Bassus and Apollonius, and of my fellow slave Zotion the deacon. May I have joy of Zotion, for he submits to the bishop as to the grace of God, and to the council of elders as to the law of Jesus Christ.
orientation: Ignatius, writing to the church in Magnesia, has just spoken of his chains and his prayer for unity, and now tells them how he came to see them through their leaders.

title: Honor the bishop as God's hidden overseer
english: It is fitting for you too not to take advantage of the bishop's age, but to give him all respect according to the power of God the Father. I have learned that the holy council of elders did not despise his apparent youthful rank, but as wise men in God yielded to him. Yet they yielded not to him, but to the Father of Jesus Christ, who is bishop of all.

So for the honor of the one who willed us, it is fitting to obey with no hypocrisy at all. For such a person does not merely deceive this bishop who is seen, but cheats the One who is unseen. And in such a matter the word is not about flesh, but about God, who knows the hidden things.
orientation: Ignatius is addressing the Magnesians, urging them to honor their bishop Damas not by his apparent youth but as one who stands in for God the Father.

title: Being Christians, not just called Christians
english: So it is fitting not only to be called Christians, but actually to be Christians. In the same way, some people call a man bishop, yet do everything apart from him. Such people do not seem to me to have a good conscience, because they do not assemble faithfully according to the commandment.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Magnesia, urging them to obey their bishop and not act apart from him.

title: Two coinages, two destinies
english: So all things are reaching their end, and two destinies lie before us: death and life. Each person is about to depart to their own place.

For it is like two kinds of coin. One belongs to God, and one belongs to the world, and each has its own stamp impressed upon it. The faithless bear the stamp of this world, but believers in love bear the stamp of God the Father through Jesus Christ. And unless we willingly choose to die into his passion, his life is not in us.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the Magnesians, urging them to live as true Christians and not merely bear the name, and now grounds this in the two possible ends before each person.

title: Unity under bishop, elders, and deacons
english: Since in the persons I have already named I saw the whole multitude in faith and loved them, I urge you: make it your aim to do everything in the concord of God. Let the bishop preside in the place of God, and the council of elders in the place of the council of the apostles, and let the deacons, who are most sweet to me, be entrusted with the service of Jesus Christ, who before the ages was with the Father and appeared at the end.

All of you, then, having taken on God's own character, respect one another, and let no one look at his neighbor according to the flesh, but always love one another in Jesus Christ. Let there be nothing in you that can divide you, but be united with the bishop and with those who preside, as a type and teaching of incorruption.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Magnesia, urging them to act in unity under their bishop, council of elders, and deacons.

title: Do nothing apart from the bishop, as the Lord did nothing apart from the Father
english: The Lord was united with the Father, and so he did nothing without the Father, neither by himself nor through the apostles. In the same way, you must do nothing without the bishop and the council of elders. Do not even try to make anything appear reasonable to you privately. Instead, gather together in one place and have one prayer, one supplication, one mind, one hope in love, in the blameless joy, which is Jesus Christ, than whom nothing is better.
All of you, run together as into one temple of God, as to one altar, to one Jesus Christ, who came forth from one Father and is one and has returned to him.
orientation: Ignatius is addressing the Magnesians, urging them to act only in unity with their bishop and elders, just as the Lord acted only in unity with the Father.

title: The prophets lived by Christ, not by Judaism
english: Do not be led astray by false teachings or by old myths, which are worthless. For if we still live according to Judaism, we are admitting that we have not received grace.

The most divine prophets lived according to Christ Jesus. That is why they were persecuted: they were inspired by his grace so that the disobedient might be fully convinced that there is one God, who revealed himself through Jesus Christ his Son, who is his Word, who came forth from silence, and who in every way pleased the one who sent him.
orientation: Ignatius is warning the Magnesians against false teachings and old myths, arguing that even the ancient prophets lived according to Jesus Christ.

title: The prophets lived by the Lord's Day and awaited Christ
english: If those who lived in the old ways came to a new hope, no longer keeping the Sabbath but living according to the Lord's day, on which our life also dawned through him and through his death, a death some deny, through which mystery we received faith, and because of this we endure, so that we may be found disciples of Jesus Christ, our only teacher, then how will we be able to live without him? Even the prophets, who were his disciples in the Spirit, awaited him as their teacher. And because of this, the one whom they righteously awaited came and raised them from the dead.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the Magnesians, arguing that Christians must no longer live according to Judaism but according to Christ, who is the new hope.

title: Live as Christians, not as Jews
english: So let us not be numb to His kindness. For if He should deal with us according to what we do, we no longer exist. Therefore, since we have become His disciples, let us learn to live according to Christianity. For whoever is called by any other name than this is not of God.

Put away, then, the evil leaven, which has grown old and turned sour, and change into new leaven, which is Jesus Christ. Be preserved in Him, so that no one among you may be corrupted, since by your fragrance you will be recognized.

It is absurd to speak of Jesus Christ and to Judaize. For Christianity did not come to faith through Judaism, but Judaism through Christianity, in which every tongue that has believed in God has been gathered together.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the Magnesians, urging them to abandon old ways and live fully as Christians in Christ.

title: Why Ignatius warns against empty glory
english: Now, my beloved, I am not writing these things because I have learned that any of you are actually in this condition. I write because, as one who is less than you, I want to guard you beforehand, so that you do not fall into the hooks of empty glory. Be fully assured instead in the birth, the passion, and the resurrection that took place in the time of the governorship of Pontius Pilate. These things were truly and certainly accomplished by Jesus Christ, our hope. May none of you ever be turned aside from Him.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the Magnesians, explaining that his warning about Judaism and false teaching is not because he knows them to be at fault, but because he wants to protect them.

title: The righteous self-accuser
english: May I benefit from you in every way, if indeed I am worthy. For even though I am in chains, I am not equal to one of you who has been set free. I know that you are not puffed up, for you have Jesus Christ within you. And what is more, when I praise you, I know that you are ashamed, as it is written: "The righteous one is his own accuser."
orientation: Ignatius, writing to the Ephesians while a prisoner, has just warned them against empty glory and now turns to his own unworthiness and their humility.

title: Be established in the Lord's teachings and submit to the bishop
english: Make every effort, then, to be established in the teachings of the Lord and the apostles, so that you may prosper in everything you do, in flesh and spirit, in faith and love, in the Son and the Father and in the Spirit, in beginning and in end, together with your most worthy bishop and the well-woven spiritual crown of your council of elders and the deacons who serve according to God.

Be subject to the bishop and to one another, as Jesus Christ was subject to the Father and the apostles were subject to Christ and to the Father, so that there may be a unity that is both fleshly and spiritual.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the Magnesians, urging them to be confirmed in the teachings of the Lord and the apostles and to submit to the bishop and one another.

title: Prayer for the Church in Syria
english: Since I know you are full of God, I have kept my exhortation brief. Remember me in your prayers, so that I may attain God and the church in Syria, from which I am not worthy to be called. For I need your prayer and love, united in God, so that the church in Syria may be deemed worthy to be refreshed with dew through your church.
orientation: Ignatius, bishop of Antioch, is writing to the church in Magnesia while being taken under guard to Rome, and here he asks for their prayers for himself and for the church in Syria.

title: Greetings from the Ephesians and other churches
english: The Ephesians who are here in Smyrna, from where I am writing to you, greet you. They are present for the glory of God, and together with Polycarp, the bishop of the Smyrnaeans, they have refreshed me in every way, just as you have. The rest of the churches also greet you in the honor of Jesus Christ. Farewell in the harmony of God, possessing an undivided spirit, who is Jesus Christ.
orientation: Ignatius is closing his letter to the Magnesians, sending greetings from the Ephesians who are with him in Smyrna and from the other churches.
